description:
Senior Associate - Venture & Growth (m/f/d)

Join the team rewriting the rules in private markets.

Moonfare delivers what few others can: the highly sought-after funds and hidden-gem investments that go beyond what most private banks offer. Every opportunity is subjected to a ruthless vetting process; the bar is unforgivingly high. The result? Institutional-quality portfolios for investors who demand more.

Our team combines finance veterans with talent from tech, consulting, law and industries you’d never expect. Headquartered in Berlin, we operate from eight offices across Europe, the US and Asia.

If you're ready to build what's next in private markets, let's talk.

Mission:

Turn Moonfare's access to the world's leading venture managers into a steady, well-underwritten flow of single-company investments our clients can actually buy.

About the role:

A significant share of Moonfare's AuM sits in venture and growth, and the direct side of it, co-investments and secondaries in VC-backed companies, is where the business is growing fastest. Right now that dealflow arrives faster than we can review it, which puts the deployment of our proprietary funds at risk and caps how far the direct platform can scale. The scope of this role begins the moment an opportunity reaches us and ends when the deal closes, so operations sits outside it, as does the client raise itself. Your first year is weighted towards screening, pipeline and diligence, with the sourcing and business development side building from there as your market view and relationships deepen. You will work alongside senior members of the team rather than alone, and what moves forward is decided together.

The team:

Venture & Growth sits inside Moonfare's Investment team and runs two connected things. One is a multi-manager vehicle making primary fund investments into leading VC and growth managers across the US and Europe, where we have historically backed Founders Fund, a16z, Accel, Lightspeed, Khosla and General Catalyst. The other is the direct programme of co-investments and secondaries that those manager relationships generate, which is where this role's centre of gravity sits. You will report to the Head of VC & Direct Investing and work daily with the commercial team, who depend on you for qualified dealflow, and alongside Legal and Operations to close deals and launch the SPVs we distribute on the platform.

You will:

  • Own the direct deal pipeline. Everything from the moment an opportunity reaches us through to close is yours to run, so nothing sits unscreened and no access window quietly closes while we are still deciding.
  • Screen inbound co-investments and secondaries, and bring a view to the team. You run the first pass on what reaches us and form a position on it. What progresses is decided together with the Head of VC & Direct Investing and the wider team, so the value of your screen lies in the quality of the argument you bring to that conversation and in how sharply you separate the two or three worth our time from the rest.
  • Run diligence on direct deals. The core of it is judgement on the business itself: how good the company is, how strong the founding team is, how large and how contested the market is, and whether the thesis survives contact with the evidence. The technical layer sits underneath, with cap table analysis, preference stacks and waterfalls, and pricing and NAV work on secondary positions, so we know exactly what we are buying and at what price. You will do this with support from senior members of the team, and contribute to primary fund diligence alongside the direct mandate.
  • Author the investment memos that go to IC. The committee decides on what you put in front of it, so a memo with a gap in it, an inaccuracy, or a risk nobody spotted becomes a decision made on the wrong basis.
  • Build the market view, and then the market position. Relationships with intermediaries, GPs and, over time, founders are what get us into constrained opportunities and keep us current on where secondaries are pricing. This part of the role grows as you do, and watching how competitors structure and go to market belongs to it, because that is what keeps us competitive on price.
  • Help make the process repeatable. You will refine how we diligence direct deals and contribute to the sourcing, screening and monitoring tooling behind it, including AI-enabled approaches, so the volume we can handle is not capped by how much a person can read.
  • Turn deals into something our clients can buy. The commercial team depends on this seat for qualified dealflow and for support packaging opportunities into investor-ready materials. Fund deployment runs at the pace this work sets.

The next Moonfarian:

  • Four or more years centred on venture and growth investing. That comes along one of two paths. Either direct investment expertise, sourcing and diligencing investments in technology companies at a venture capital, growth equity or crossover fund, or an allocator seat focused on VC and growth where you have underwritten co-investments hands-on. Directly relevant adjacent backgrounds include TMT and technology investment banking, tech-focused private equity or software buyout, corporate development or corporate VC at a technology company, and consulting with a tech or commercial diligence focus. What matters most is a demonstrable track record of hands-on deal work: screening opportunities, running diligence, and taking a view through to a decision.
  • A network in venture you can already use. This one is non-negotiable. Relationships with GPs, intermediaries such as placement agents and bankers, and other LPs and co-investors, enough to get us access to constrained opportunities, support diligence and track spin-out candidates. You do not need the network of someone twice your experience. You do need a real one, and you will build a much larger one here.
  • Investment judgement you can defend. You form a view on a company and argue it, including the case against. You can read a business and a founding team, size a market and test a thesis against what the evidence actually supports. You are genuinely fluent in emerging technology and can develop conviction on themes and business models, with AI front of mind but not the only lens. You assess attractiveness quickly on limited or imperfect information, you are comfortable with financial modelling and market analysis, and you know your way around cap tables, preference stacks and waterfalls, secondary pricing, VC term sheets and SPV mechanics. You can hold several live opportunities at once and prioritise sharply between them.
  • An entrepreneurial instinct, which matters here as much as the investing. This one is non-negotiable too. This is a builder's seat as much as an investor's. You want a hand in structuring, go-to-market, process design and the operational scaffolding of a business line that is still being built. Your AI fluency goes past using the tools to designing processes around them.
  • Communication that works in three different rooms, and relationships that outlast any one deal. You can pitch and tailor to an investment committee, to a commercial team, and to clients, and prepare the reports and presentations each of them needs. Just as important is what you build over time with GPs and intermediaries, the standing that makes them think of us when something scarce comes up, because that is what turns a contact list into access. Excellent written and spoken English is essential.

How the role is measured: 

  • Deals sourced, screened, and taken through to IC.
  • Timely deployment of Moonfare's proprietary funds, such as the Moonfare Technology Fund.
  • Allocation secured with GPs and intermediaries, meaning access we would not otherwise have had.
  • Whether IC can decide on your memos without rework, and whether risks surface in diligence rather than after close.
  • Capital raised on direct deals and the performance ultimately generated. These are programme outcomes you contribute to rather than own alone, and they are read that way.

What success looks like:

By six months, the deal pipeline runs without the Head of VC & Direct Investing having to chase it. Opportunities are screened as they arrive, you are bringing a formed view on each one to the team, and the queue is visible to everyone who needs it.|
By twelve months, deal review is fully operationalised, with a process the team can run rather than one person's habits, and more than ten direct deals have been through IC.

This role is unlikely to be a good match if you

  • Prefer to let relationships develop slowly and mostly in writing. Much of our access comes from conversations with managers and intermediaries you do not know yet, and someone reserved about starting them will find the sourcing half of this job hard going.
  • Want a defined process to work inside. A good part of what this role runs does not exist yet, and you would be designing it while live deals are moving.
  • Want sole authority over what you invest in. We discuss deals as a team and decide together what progresses, which means your view gets argued with before it gets acted on. If you want to run your own book without that, this will frustrate you.

What your growth could look like:

The next step from here is Associate Principal. Getting there means leading the majority of diligence processes rather than running them with support, and having a network that generates opportunities rather than one that keeps you informed.

What you get here that you would not get at a fund: you join the Head of VC & Direct Investing in GP conversations from early on and inherit access to a built-up base of manager relationships. You see the commercial side of raising capital for a deal alongside the investment side, which most investors never touch. And you help build a wider business, across a discretionary fund, capital raising for individual deals and, in time, a secondary market.

If you feel you do not meet all of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply!

We can only accept applications from those eligible to live and work in Berlin/London. This is a hybrid role with office attendance required 4 days/week.

Please note that we do not accept applications sent by email. You should submit your application directly through our careers website.

Invest in Yourself:

  • Ownership and Impact: You are empowered to bring ideas, make decisions, and see your work directly contribute to Moonfare's success.
  • Transparent Environment: We believe in open communication. You will receive regular updates on company strategy, performance against our KPIs, and key business decisions.
  • Personal Growth: We support your development with an individual growth budget of €1,500 or 2% of your base salary (whichever is higher).
  • Invest in Your Future: We support your long-term financial goals with a company pension scheme, providing a 20% employer contribution.
  • Relax and Recharge: You start with 25 vacation days and you’ll receive one additional day for each year of tenure, up to a maximum of 30 days. Moonfare gifts two days during our annual end of year company shutdown.
  • Daily Lunch: Enjoy a free lunch every day that you are in the Berlin office, with a weekly changing menu that includes salads, curries, pastas, and a variety of vegan and vegetarian options.
  • Subsidised Public Transport: We support your commute with a monthly subsidy for the Deutschland job ticket, making your travel easier and more affordable.
  • Fitness and Wellbeing: Stay active with a subsidised Urban Sports Club membership, giving you flexible access to a wide variety of sports and wellness activities across Germany.
  • A Culture of Excellence: Join a team of ambitious, smart, and committed professionals who are passionate about revolutionising private market investing.
  • Performance Reward: As a performance-first company, we reward strong performance twice a year, so your impact translates directly into how your pay grows - through potential base salary increases and/or bonuses.

Our Values:

  • Our clients come first, Moonfare comes second, and we prioritise ourselves third - Client-Centric Focus. Putting clients first means creating value for them is essential. Placing Moonfare second signifies that our individual professional future at Moonfare depends on the company's commercial success. Prioritising ourselves third reflects our humility in putting clients and Moonfare before personal interests.
  • We pursue excellence and honor our promises - Commitment to Excellence. We hold ourselves to the highest standards, taking responsibility for our failures, and celebrating our successes. We commit to deadlines and stick to them and we learn from our mistakes.
  • We are here to win and to celebrate our collective achievements - Win together. We are mission-focused and think and act like owners. We exemplify the attitude we expect and each of us commits to do what it takes to succeed.
  • We foster personal growth but each of us earns our place as a Moonfarian through merit - Growth and Merit. We hire, retain, and develop exceptional people and invest in empowering them to excel. We must all earn our place at the table every day.

We understand the important role that diversity plays in our success. Different backgrounds, experiences and ideas push us further and raise the bar. We’re committed to developing an inclusive and safe culture where everyone - regardless of colour, race, religion, sex, origin, sexuality, disability, marital status, citizenship or gender identity - knows that they are an integral part of the team and can bring their full potential to their work.

Either direct investment expertise, sourcing and diligencing investments in technology companies at a venture capital, growth equity or crossover fund, or an allocator seat focused on VC and growth where you have underwritten co-investments hands-on. Directly relevant adjacent backgrounds include TMT and technology investment banking, tech-focused private equity or software buyout, corporate development or corporate VC at a technology company, and consulting with a tech or commercial diligence focus. What matters most is a demonstrable track record of hands-on deal work: screening opportunities, running diligence, and taking a view through to a decision.
  • A network in venture you can already use. This one is non-negotiable. Relationships with GPs, intermediaries such as placement agents and bankers, and other LPs and co-investors, enough to get us access to constrained opportunities, support diligence and track spin-out candidates. You do not need the network of someone twice your experience. You do need a real one, and you will build a much larger one here.
  • Investment judgement you can defend. You form a view on a company and argue it, including the case against. You can read a business and a founding team, size a market and test a thesis against what the evidence actually supports. You are genuinely fluent in emerging technology and can develop conviction on themes and business models, with AI front of mind but not the only lens. You assess attractiveness quickly on limited or imperfect information, you are comfortable with financial modelling and market analysis, and you know your way around cap tables, preference stacks and waterfalls, secondary pricing, VC term sheets and SPV mechanics. You can hold several live opportunities at once and prioritise sharply between them.
  • An entrepreneurial instinct, which matters here as much as the investing. This one is non-negotiable too. This is a builder's seat as much as an investor's. You want a hand in structuring, go-to-market, process design and the operational scaffolding of a business line that is still being built. Your AI fluency goes past using the tools to designing processes around them.
  • Communication that works in three different rooms, and relationships that outlast any one deal. You can pitch and tailor to an investment committee, to a commercial team, and to clients, and prepare the reports and presentations each of them needs. Just as important is what you build over time with GPs and intermediaries, the standing that makes them think of us when something scarce comes up, because that is what turns a contact list into access. Excellent written and spoken English is essential.

How the role is measured: 

  • Deals sourced, screened, and taken through to IC.
  • Timely deployment of Moonfare's proprietary funds, such as the Moonfare Technology Fund.
  • Allocation secured with GPs and intermediaries, meaning access we would not otherwise have had.
  • Whether IC can decide on your memos without rework, and whether risks surface in diligence rather than after close.
  • Capital raised on direct deals and the performance ultimately generated. These are programme outcomes you contribute to rather than own alone, and they are read that way.

What success looks like:

By six months, the deal pipeline runs without the Head of VC & Direct Investing having to chase it. Opportunities are screened as they arrive, you are bringing a formed view on each one to the team, and the queue is visible to everyone who needs it.|
By twelve months, deal review is fully operationalised, with a process the team can run rather than one person's habits, and more than ten direct deals have been through IC.

This role is unlikely to be a good match if you

  • Prefer to let relationships develop slowly and mostly in writing. Much of our access comes from conversations with managers and intermediaries you do not know yet, and someone reserved about starting them will find the sourcing half of this job hard going.
  • Want a defined process to work inside. A good part of what this role runs does not exist yet, and you would be designing it while live deals are moving.
  • Want sole authority over what you invest in. We discuss deals as a team and decide together what progresses, which means your view gets argued with before it gets acted on. If you want to run your own book without that, this will frustrate you.

What your growth could look like:

The next step from here is Associate Principal. Getting there means leading the majority of diligence processes rather than running them with support, and having a network that generates opportunities rather than one that keeps you informed.

What you get here that you would not get at a fund: you join the Head of VC & Direct Investing in GP conversations from early on and inherit access to a built-up base of manager relationships. You see the commercial side of raising capital for a deal alongside the investment side, which most investors never touch. And you help build a wider business, across a discretionary fund, capital raising for individual deals and, in time, a secondary market.

If you feel you do not meet all of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply!

We can only accept applications from those eligible to live and work in Berlin/London. This is a hybrid role with office attendance required 4 days/week.

Please note that we do not accept applications sent by email. You should submit your application directly through our careers website.

description:
Senior Linux Administrator

Cambridge, UK | Full-time | Permanent | Hybrid 

Salary: £60,000 to £70,000 + Bonus + Equity

The salary range for this role is broad, as we are able to consider varying levels of experience.  Any offer made will carefully take into account level of experience (including relevant industry experience), transferable relevant skills and previous relevant achievements.

About us 

Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in material and climate science, to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved.  Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent and passion.  

Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast.  

About the role 

Riverlane is looking for an experienced Linux administrator to own and grow our core computational infrastructure. This is a hands-on role combining day-to-day administration of our High-Performance Computing (HPC) environment with longer-term planning, automation, and improvement of our infrastructure estate.

You'll be the primary owner of our HPC cluster and core Linux infrastructure, working closely with IT management and wider Infrastructure Team to keep systems reliable today while building towards a more resilient, scalable environment for tomorrow.

Key Responsibilities

HPC Cluster Administration

  • Administer and maintain the HPC cluster, including compute nodes, storage systems, and networking.
  • Evaluate and evolve cluster topology, compute node configuration, and hardware resource utilisation as the estate grows.
  • Lead the deployment, configuration, and troubleshooting of HPC tooling, particularly Slurm — including queue structures and job scheduling policies.
  • Monitor system performance and ensure high availability of HPC resources, using observability tools such as Prometheus; investigate anomalies and outages.
  • Assess and maintain the network file storage solution for throughput, scalability, and latency.

Business As Usual (BAU) Administration

  • Maintain, patch, and troubleshoot core Linux infrastructure (RHEL).
  • Act as an escalation point for complex technical issues raised by the Riverlane team.
  • Provide operational upkeep of core infrastructure, including servers, tooling, and licence managers.
  • Maintain Synopsys EDA tooling, including licence server management, environment configuration, and performance optimisation for electronic design automation workflows.
  • Provide sound technical support to users of the HPC environment.
  • Improve self-service capability for users, enabling routine tasks (e.g. restarting VNC sessions, resetting passwords) to be performed without engineering intervention.

Automation & Enhancement

  • Automate routine tasks using scripting and infrastructure-as-code tools (Bash, Python, Ansible).
  • Collaborate with the Infrastructure Team to plan and implement improvements to HPC infrastructure.
  • Own work packages and deliver them within agreed sprint windows.
  • Build and maintain documentation for systems, processes, and configurations.
  • Communicate effectively with stakeholders on progress and delivered improvements.

Security, Compliance & Resilience

  • Ensure security and compliance across the HPC estate, including security hardening and lifecycle management.
  • Maintain and develop the off-site backup strategy, ensuring data integrity, disaster recovery readiness, and compliance with data retention policies.

Requirements & Experience

  • Extensive experience administering and growing infrastructure in fast-paced engineering environments.
  • Enterprise Linux expertise: deep knowledge of Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) administration, security hardening, lifecycle management, and troubleshooting.
  • Hands-on experience configuring, scaling, tuning, and troubleshooting job schedulers (e.g. Slurm) and distributed compute environments.
  • Strong understanding of network file storage protocols and network optimisation for computational workloads.
  • Proficient with container environments and virtualisation infrastructure.
  • High proficiency with infrastructure automation tools (Ansible, Python, Bash) and infrastructure-as-code practices.
  • Experience with backup and disaster recovery strategy and implementation.
  • Experience managing licensed EDA or similar specialist software tooling (e.g. Synopsys) is a strong plus.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to support both technical and non-technical users and translate complex issues into clear guidance.

What can you expect from us 

  • A comprehensive benefits package that includes an annual bonus plan, private medical insurance, life insurance, and a contributory pension scheme 
  • Equity, so that our team can share in the long-term success of Riverlane  
  • 28 days annual leave, plus bank holidays and enhanced family leave 
  • A diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 20 different nationalities 
  • A learning environment that encourages individual, team and company growth and development, including a regular programme of learning events and training and conference budgets 

How to apply 

Please upload a CV and covering letter by clicking 'Apply'. Your covering letter should explain why you are applying for the job and what skills and experience you can bring to the role. 

We review CVs as we receive them and interview as soon as we have applications that look like a good match. We do not use closing dates. So, please apply as soon as possible to avoid missing out on this role. 

If you have any queries, please contact com. 

Everyone is welcome at Riverlane. We are an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from eligible and suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender reassignment, religion or belief, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, or pregnancy and maternity/paternity. 

Women and other underrepresented groups may be less likely to apply for a role unless they meet all or nearly all of the requirements.  If this applies to you, we still encourage you to apply - you may be a great fit, even if you don’t meet every single qualification. We’d love to hear from you. 

If you need any adjustments made to the application or selection process so you can do your best, please let us know. We will be happy to help.

GDPR notice: Riverlane collects and processes personal data in accordance with applicable data protection laws. If you are a European Job Applicant see the privacy notice for further details.

Your Impact at LILA

We're building a talent-dense, high-agency AI safety team at Lila that will engage all core teams within the organization (science, model training, lab integration, etc.), to identify and mitigate risks from scientific superintelligence while retaining the core scientific discovery capabilities of the stack. The initial focus of this team will be to build and implement a bespoke safety strategy for Lila, tailored to its specific goals and deployment strategies. This will involve technical safety strategy development, broader ecosystem engagement, safety-focused evaluations, safety systems to mitigate risks, and a research agenda that explores longer-term needs such as oversight of superintelligent scientific systems.

We are seeking a chemist to map risk across the chemical sciences domain: you will connect deep chemistry expertise with dual-use risk assessment to help safeguard increasingly capable scientific AI. You will investigate how advances in chemical research could change harmful capabilities, including established and emerging chemical threats.

What You'll Be Building

  • Map chemical misuse risks across scientific models, agents and automated experimentation, connecting scientific advances to harmful applications and identifying emerging or overlooked pathways.
  • Assess how scientific feasibility, practical complexity and actors' expertise or resources affect the plausibility and likelihood of misuse, including which constraints AI could change.
  • Distinguish established capabilities, plausible future developments and weakly supported hypotheses, updating assessments as scientific evidence and AI capabilities evolve.
  • Identify gaps in coverage, frame questions for consultants and specialist organizations, and assess and integrate their findings with support from the expert-program team.
  • Translate scientific risk judgments into dual-use policy boundaries, evaluation priorities and mitigation requirements that preserve beneficial chemistry.
  • Partner with threat modelers, evaluation researchers and mitigation teams to design informative assessments, interpret red-team findings and test safeguards.

What You'll Need to Succeed

  • Deep expertise (a PhD, or comparable experience) in synthetic chemistry or a closely related discipline, demonstrated through substantial research or applied work and sound interpretation of experimental evidence. This includes a background in molecular design and medicinal chemistry, inorganic and organometallic chemistry, synthesis, process development and formulations, or other relevant sub-fields.
  • Substantive experience assessing chemical dual-use risks (e.g. across national security, export controls, or other chemical risk tracking such as the CWC).
  • Strong scientific judgment about feasibility, uncertainty and practical constraints, including the ability to investigate unfamiliar questions and recognize the limits of your expertise.
  • The ability to identify appropriate specialists, critically assess their evidence and combine findings across disciplines into defensible risk assessments.
  • Clear scientific communication, independent research judgment and an ability to collaborate across science, engineering and policy.

Bonus Points For

  • Prior experience applying domain expertise to AI safety through one or more of: scientific analysis informing threat models; evaluation or red-teaming work; or mitigation design.
  • Experience commissioning specialist research or coordinating external scientific collaborators.
  • Experience with automated chemistry, scientific modeling or the translation of computational findings into physical experiments.

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

International Benefits. Full-time employees outside the U.S. receive a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region. USD salary ranges apply only to U.S.-based positions; international salaries are set to local market.

Expected Base Salary Range
$148,000—$208,000 USD

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

We’re All In

Today the honest answer to "is this build safe?" is "it worked on the test robot." You will replace that with a system: the simulation environment the team tests against, the regression suites that run on every change, the hardware-in-the-loop rigs, and the release gates that decide whether a build can go onto a robot that will patrol a customer site alone tonight. This is the first engineer dedicated to reliability and test infrastructure, and it sits in our Robot Autonomy team, next to the engineers building perception, localisation, planning and locomotion. Hardware-in-the-loop: bench rigs and test procedures on the physical robots for what simulation cannot tell you. Failure injection: drop sensors, degrade LiDAR returns, kill the network link, corrupt odometry, then verify the system degrades and recovers the way we tell customers it does. Field incidents to tests: when a robot misbehaves on site, reproduce it deterministically and turn it into a permanent regression test. ABOUT THE ROLE

description:
Staff Digital Product Designer – E-Commerce / Web Platform

Department: E-Commerce & Customer Experience / Web Team

Level: Individual Contributor Lead (Staff Level)

Location: Lille / Paris 

1. Context & Project

Decathlon's purpose is to bring people together through sport to make wellbeing accessible for all, guiding our overarching ambition to build a Local Human Bond and deliver accessible, unique sporting solutions globally. In this context, our goal is to build personalized, enriched experiences across all digital touchpoints and physical stores, leveraging Digital, Data, and AI to elevate the global customer journey.

The E-Commerce Web Challenge

As the digital front door for millions of sport practice enthusiasts around the globe, our web platform (decathlon.country) must seamlessly convert online curiosity into real-world sport experiences. Our challenge is to transform a massive, multi-category web store into an intuitive, frictionless digital portal.

We need to guide every user—from a first-time visitor searching for sports goods to a returning member—through a smooth journey that connects online browsing directly with local store availability, click-and-collect, and circular services like rentals and repairs.

By building a standardized, modular web experience, we equip country teams and international franchise partners with pre-validated, high-converting funnel journeys so they can scale local commerce effortlessly without rebuilding core web experiences from scratch.

Scope & Structure (4 Dedicated E-Com Squads)

  1. Acquisition: Turn global internet users into active visitors through high-converting landing experiences, SEO, campaign entry points, and personalized traffic onboarding.
  2. Navigation: Help users find the exact product or advice they need within a vast catalog through intelligent search, taxonomy, filtering, and catalog hierarchy.
  3. Decision: Give users every compelling reason to choose a product using rich product detail pages (PDP), media, sizing confidence, customer reviews, and circular/sustainability options.
  4. Conversion: Deliver frictionless checkout, flexible payment methods, order self-tracking, store pickup options, and effortless returns.

2. Your Mission

As a Staff Digital Product Designer, you operate as a principal individual contributor and strategic leader within the Decathlon E-Commerce team. Operating with high autonomy on complex, cross-squad web challenges, you shape our long-term 

E-Commerce Web Experience Vision.

You will work in close triad leadership with Staff Engineering and Staff Product Managers (GPMs), while partnering hand-in-hand with a dedicated UX Researcher (UXR) as your main practice partner to ground every design decision in deep user insights and quantitative data.

Beyond defining strategy, you lead hands-on experimentation, product de-risking, and rapid validation loops—ensuring high-stakes web features across Acquisition, Navigation, Decision, and Conversion are proven through A/B testing, CRO analysis, and real user data before global rollout. You align the 4 web squads around a unified web vision, accelerate commercial value delivery, and elevate design craft maturity across teams.

3. What You’ll Do

Strategic Alignment & Web Funnel Vision

  • Triad Leadership: Partner closely with Staff Engineers, Staff PMs, and your dedicated UXR partner to define long-term roadmaps, tech feasibility, and strategic UX priorities across squads.
  • Web Experience Strategy: Define and advocate for the long-term web design strategy, establishing web principles that influence product and commercial roadmaps.
  • 4-Squad Orchestration: Drive alignment across the Acquisition, Navigation, Decision, and Conversion squads to ensure a cohesive end-to-end web journey without siloed user friction.
  • Priority Segment Focus: Set strategic web UX direction tailored to key user segments (Families, New Customers, Members), driving personalization and context-aware landing journeys.
  • Macro Metrics Tracking: Track and optimize web performance metrics across the full funnel: SEO Traffic, CTR, Search Success, Add-to-Cart Rate, Conversion Rate, and Retention.

Product De-Risking & Web Experimentation Strategy

  • Research Partner Alignment: Work hand-in-hand with UXR to formulate hypotheses, map user knowledge gaps, and design research strategies for complex e-commerce flows.
  • De-Risking Frameworks: Formulate and drive product de-risking strategies for high-impact web initiatives—identifying usability, commercial, and technical risks early in discovery.
  • Concrete Web Experimentation: Design and execute hands-on A/B tests, multivariate testing, CRO experiments, and prototype usability tests across the 4 squads to validate hypotheses before engineering rollouts.
  • Data-Informed Decisions: Partner with Data & Analytics leads to build quantitative testing frameworks, leveraging web analytics to guide roadmap trade-offs.
  • Testing Culture Elevation: Coach web product squads on hypothesis formulation, CRO best practices, and rapid build-measure-learn loops.

4. Role & Responsibilities (Skills & Behaviors)

 

Craft / Technical Skills

  • Research & Web Strategy: Partner closely with our UXR to enrich foundational customer knowledge (B2C web journeys) and co-define a CX vision to build collective alignment across stakeholders.
  • Problem Discovery: Uncover drop-off points across the 4 squads through quantitative funnel analytics and qualitative research; structure decisions using Opportunity Solution Trees (OST).
  • Solution Discovery: Explore and prototype web interfaces early and often; design high-converting, accessible, and responsive layouts connected to our Design System.
  • Testing & CRO: Continuously de-risk solution feasibility, usability, and conversion lift using context-tailored testing tools (A/B testing, user testing, CRO analytics).
  • AI Exploration: Test and integrate AI tools (e.g., generative search, smart recommendations, automated layout testing) to amplify design and research workflows.

Behaviors / Soft Skills

  • Leadership & Strategic Collaboration: Lead cross-squad web taskforces alongside Staff Engineering and Staff PMs, make sound decisions under partial data, and support the Design Manager in org planning and hiring committees.
  • Influence & Emotional Intelligence: Work proactively across PMs, Engineering Managers, and Business Leads to shape priorities using emotional intelligence and data-backed storytelling.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Involve engineering, data, UXR, and SEO teams early in the design process to create a psychologically safe, feedback-rich environment.
  • Design Mentoring: Elevate the web design practice by mentoring 3–4 designers, facilitating cross-squad design critiques, and connecting design solutions across teams.
  • Growth Mindset: Turn failed A/B experiments into collective learning opportunities and maintain a structured personal growth plan.

5. Why Join the E-Commerce Web Team?

Challenges You Will Tackle

  • High-Scale Web Impact: Optimizing a global web platform handling millions of daily visits across dozens of international markets.
  • 4-Squad Synergy: Unifying Acquisition, Navigation, Decision, and Conversion into one fluid, frictionless web journey.
  • Strong Triad Partnership: Working in direct alignment with Staff Engineering, Staff PMs, and a dedicated UXR partner to shape high-level product strategy.
  • Performance & Accessibility at Scale: Designing lightweight, lightning-fast web pages that meet strict WCAG accessibility and SEO benchmarks.

 

This Role Is a Perfect Match for You If…

  • You thrive on de-risking web journeys via A/B testing and CRO data rather than subjective opinions.
  • You excel at triad collaboration with Staff Tech and Staff PMs, backed by deep research partnership with UXR.
  • You enjoy orchestrating design across multiple squads (Acquisition through Conversion) to deliver a unified customer experience.
  • You balance commercial conversion into  goals with high design standards and accessibility.
  • You love mentoring designers and upskilling teams in experimentation, data literacy, and web craft excellence.

 

 

DECATHLON DIGITAL CONTEXT 

What if technology allowed us to push the boundaries and take sports experiences to new levels? That's exactly our goal at Decathlon Digital! We are a team of 5,000+ experts in software engineering, product management, data, cloud, and cybersecurity, distributed across Paris, Lille, and Amsterdam. Together, we are creating the largest digital sports platform, leveraging tech innovation from design to value chain optimization, connected experiences and product second life.


Changing the game for good. We are in this for the love of sports. And like everything we love, we want it to last. That’s why we are embarking on a journey to create a more sustainable tech model, reducing our direct environmental impact while maintaining a safe, diverse, and inclusive space for all our people to learn and thrive together. Team up with us to design the digital future of sports.

As a Supply Planner at HelloFresh, you will play a key role in ensuring our customers receive the highest-quality ingredients—on time, in full, every week. You’ll manage a portfolio of European suppliers within our Conventional Cluster and work closely with Production, Quality, Menu Planning, and Procurement to keep our supply chain running smoothly. You will thrive in a fast-moving environment where data-driven decisions, continuous improvement, and customer centricity are at the heart of everything we do.

Note: This is a 6-month fixed-term position, with the potential for extension based on business needs.

  • Manage the end-to-end purchase order process for your assigned supplier portfolio, ensuring timely and accurate deliveries.

  • Support weekly operational planning by validating forecasts, assessing risks, and proposing mitigation strategies.
  • Identify and implement process improvements to strengthen supply chain efficiency and prevent recurring issues.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to secure ingredient availability for upcoming menus and promotional volumes.

What You’ll Bring: Your Ingredients

  • Experience in supply planning, procurement, logistics, or a similar operational role.
  • Strong analytical skills and proficiency with Excel or other data tools.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and collaboratively.
  • A structured and proactive working style, with the ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities.

Above all, we are looking for people who will make HelloFresh better. Skills develop in many ways, and we value diverse experiences. Even if you don’t check every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

  • Connect with the team at our annual offsite event and festive "Back to School" and Christmas parties.

Are you the missing ingredient? If this sounds like a tasty opportunity, we’d be excited to hear from you. We aim to review your profile and respond within 5 business days.

description:
The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify’s text-to-speech products to turn whatever they’re reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

With the growth of our Android app, being the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, we find the need for a Senior Android Engineer to help us support the new user base as well as work on new and exciting projects to push us forward.   

This is a key role and ideal for someone who thinks strategically, enjoys fast-paced environments, passionate about making product decisions, and has experience building great user experiences that delight users.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount. 

Our interview process involves several technical interviews and we aim to complete them within 1 week. 

What You’ll Do

  • Owning major features and working closely with our design team - take ownership of features inside the app and become responsible of delivering high quality features
  • Shape the future of our Android team
  • Own, maintain and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Participate in discussions across different teams - Product, Design, Engineering
  • Review pull requests, and support other teammates
  • Handle critical issues or cope with unexpected challenges 
  • Take ownership of feature releases and provide nightly builds for the QA team

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience
  • Familiarity with Android components
  • Experience building or contributing to at least one Android app
  • Product design intuition and user empathy
  • Drive to push the boundaries of Android UI/UX
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing tests
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase above and beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Rock solid experience with Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android Animations, Jetpack Navigation, JUnit tests
  • Excellent communication skills
  • User oriented problem solving approach
  • Driven with continuous feedback from leaders

Bonus:

  • Experience building, maintaining, or otherwise contributing to open source projects in Android
  • Experience with iOS, Web or NodeJS

Technologies we use:

  • Kotlin
  • Kotlin Coroutines
  • Kotlin Flow
  • Jetpack Navigation
  • Dagger 2
  • Room
  • Custom Views, Canvas & Paint
  • Jetpack Compose
  • JUnit

What We offer:

  • A fast-growing environment where you can help shape the company and product.
  • An entrepreneurial-minded team that supports risk, intuition, and hustle.
  • A hands-off management approach so you can focus and do your best work.
  • An opportunity to make a big impact in a transformative industry.
  • Competitive salaries, a friendly and laid-back atmosphere, and a commitment to building a great asynchronous culture.
  • Opportunity to work on a life-changing product that millions of people use.
  • Build products that directly impact and support people with learning differences like dyslexia, ADD, low vision, concussions, autism, and more.
  • Work in one of the fastest growing sectors of tech, the intersection of artificial intelligence and audio.

The France Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-100,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit? 

Refer them!

In this role you will work hands-on across the knowledge graph lifecycle from ingestion through modeling, curation, implementation, integration, and deployment. Enable faster solution development by providing high-quality, well-documented data foundations. Experience working with relational and graph-based data models. Familiarity with semantic modeling concepts, ontologies, or knowledge graphs (e.g., RDF/OWL concepts). title: Knowledge Engineering Manager

description: We Are: Accenture is a global professional services and solutions company that helps leading organizations reinvent with digital, cloud, data, and AI capabilities, drawing on its large global workforce, industry expertise, and ecosystem partnerships to create 360° value. By combining hands-on engineering with deep industry context, we help organizations build their digital core, modernize operations, unlock value from data and AI, and deliver tangible business outcomes at speed and scale. You Are: We are looking for a Back-End Engineer to design, build, and operate the data infrastructure and services that power our AI-driven knowledge platform. You will work across the full back-end stack — architecting APIs, building data pipelines, managing multi-modal database systems, and owning the reliability and performance of the services that application and product teams depend on. You bring strong engineering fundamentals and are equally comfortable designing a relational schema, tuning a graph query, standing up a vector store, or shipping a production-grade REST API. Knowledge graph and semantic technology experience is central to this role, but the work extends across the broader data and service layer: ingestion, transformation, storage, retrieval, and delivery at enterprise scale. Key Responsibilities: Hydrate structured and semi-structured data into Knowledge Graphs by mapping source data to ontology models. Develop data mapping and transformation workflows using R2RML or similar technologies. Write and optimize SPARQL queries for graph loading, validation, and retrieval. Build and maintain data ingestion pipelines and integrate data from enterprise systems. Design and optimize relational database schemas and queries to support efficient graph hydration and ETL workflows. Deploy, configure, and maintain vector database infrastructure for embedding storage, indexing, and semantic retrieval at scale. Design and maintain scalable graph query APIs consumed by internal application and product teams. Performance-tune graph database queries, indexing strategies, and data access patterns. Own containerization, deployment, and monitoring of graph services in cloud environments. Ensure data quality, ontology alignment, and secure handling of sensitive data (PII/PHI). Collaborate with ontologists, architects, and application teams to support Knowledge Graph implementations. This role is hybrid in nature and will require time in office and traveling to client locations. Travel can be between 20-80% Here's What You Need: Minimum 3 years experience in Knowledge Graph data hydration and ontology-based data mapping, including strong understanding of RDF, SPARQL, and semantic technologies. Minimum 3 years experience with R2RML or similar mapping frameworks for transforming relational data into graph models. Minimum 3 years experience with graph databases (e.g., StarDog, GraphWise, Neo4J), along with Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. including strong SQL proficiency. Minimum 3 years hands-on experience with relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQL Server), including schema design, indexing, and query optimization. Minimum 3 years experience deploying and operating vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, or Qdrant) in production environments. description: We are: The Advanced Technology Centers (ATCs) are the engine for reinvention in our clients’ transformation journey. Powered by more than 255,000 people across 24 countries, ATCs provide our clients with seamless access to industry insights and innovative technology solutions. Stronger together! The Advanced Technology Centers (ATCs) make a tremendous impact in solving our clients’ business problems by leveraging innovation, intelligence, industry insights, new IT, and new technology skills. With the global environment changing at a faster pace, our clients are facing unprecedented challenges, and they need us more than ever before. As a Network, ATCs are positioned to unlock greater opportunities and exponential value for our clients. The value for our clients and our people: For our clients, the Network provides the strength of our geographic diversity, greater resilience, and seamless access to the deepest industry knowledge, the latest in Gen AI solutions, and tech expertise from around the world. For our people, it brings an opportunity to shape truly boundaryless career paths in a highly collaborative team of experts where they can learn from each other and solve the world’s most complex client challenges. You Are You are a Knowledge Architect at the intersection of semantic AI and agentic systems — shaping the knowledge backbone of AI platforms by designing the ontologies, graphs, and data models that enable intelligent agents to reason, plan, and act. You are equally comfortable whiteboarding an ontology with a domain expert and pushing graph schemas to production alongside an ML team. You see the world as a graph, and you believe that well-structured knowledge is the foundation of truly intelligent machines. You thrive on translating complex, messy real-world knowledge into clean, reasoned, machine-readable structures that AI agents can act on — and you bring the rigor, curiosity, and collaboration to do it at scale. The Work You will embed directly with clients as a trusted technology advisor and hands-on engineer — leading the architecture and development of knowledge graphs, ontologies, and semantic data models that power next-generation agentic AI systems at enterprise scale. Responsabilities Own the end-to-end design, governance, and maintenance of enterprise-scale knowledge graphs and ontologies, bridging structured domain knowledge with large-scale agentic AI pipelines to enable reasoning, planning, and decision-making. Develop and govern ontologies, taxonomies, and semantic data models that formalize domain knowledge and support interoperability across systems and teams. Define and enforce data modeling standards, schema design patterns, and best practices for structured and semi-structured knowledge representation. Translate complex domain knowledge from subject matter experts into formal, machine-readable knowledge structures using RDF, OWL, SPARQL, or property graph models. Lead knowledge engineering discovery workshops and working sessions with client stakeholders to surface, validate, and formalize domain knowledge requirements. Collaborate with AI/ML engineers to integrate knowledge graphs as grounding and context layers for LLM-based agentic pipelines and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. Design knowledge structures that support multi-step agent reasoning, tool use, and dynamic planning across heterogeneous data sources. Work with project teams, team leaders, delivery leads, and client stakeholders to create standout Data & AI offerings powered by graph-based technologies. Collaborate with data engineering and platform teams to build scalable pipelines for knowledge graph population, enrichment, and lifecycle management. Develop strong client relationships and earn the trust of key stakeholders as a strategic advisor. Communicate complex ontological concepts and graph architectures clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. Evaluate and pilot emerging tools, frameworks, and standards (e.g., LPG vs. RDF, Wikidata, schema.org, W3C standards). title: Knowledge Engineering Senior Manager (all genders)

description: About the Centre for Advanced Data APAC The Centre for Advanced Data (C4AD) is Accenture's specialist centre of excellence that sets the architecture standard for modern, AI-ready data estates across APAC, and mobilises the talent to deliver them at scale. The C4AD operates across three core disciplines: Master Data Architecture, Knowledge Engineering, and Data Products. Every practitioner in the C4AD is expected to apply agentic and generative techniques as the default way of working, not as an add-on. The centre supports large-scale data and AI transformation programmes across the region, ranging from enterprise data modernisation to AI-ready platform builds. Job Description Join the Centre for Advanced Data APAC as a Knowledge Engineer, where you will own ontology and semantic strategy across engagements, set the knowledge-engineering standards for the practice, and assure the semantic layers that ground enterprise AI. You will define how the C4AD approaches knowledge representation across programmes, and hold the line on quality, consistency, and semantic integrity as those programmes scale. You will work closely with Data Architects and AI Engineers, ensuring that the ontologies and knowledge graphs you define and govern give AI systems something real, structured, and reliable to reason over. Project Description / Key Responsibilities Own ontology and semantic strategy across C4AD engagements, setting the approach, standards, and quality bar for knowledge engineering across the practice. Assure semantic layers that ground enterprise AI, reviewing, governing, and signing off on the ontological structures that AI systems in our programmes reason over. Design, develop, and govern enterprise ontologies, taxonomies, and knowledge graphs that accurately represent business domains, their relationships, and the rules that govern them. Build and govern semantic models using RDF/OWL, SHACL, and SPARQL, and property graph approaches using platforms such as Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, or Stardog. Apply and adapt industry-standard ontologies (e.g. FIBO, BIAN, GS1, TM Forum) to meet organisation-specific semantic requirements. Develop and enforce semantic modelling standards, naming conventions, versioning, and curation workflows, and drive adoption of those standards across delivery teams. Enable AI and ML applications through knowledge graph enrichment, entity resolution, semantic search, and ontology-powered RAG pipelines. Engage business SMEs and domain experts to elicit and formalise implicit business rules, relationships, and concepts into explicit ontological structures. Key Skills 5+ years of experience in knowledge engineering, ontology design, or semantic modelling, with a track record of owning the knowledge engineering approach on complex programmes, not just contributing to it. Proven deep expertise in ontology engineering, authoring OWL ontologies, RDFS schemas, SHACL constraint shapes, and SPARQL queries, with real enterprise delivery behind it. Hands-on experience with graph databases and knowledge graph platforms such as Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, Stardog, or GraphDB. Proficiency with semantic tooling including Protégé, TopBraid Composer, or equivalent ontology authoring environments. Strong understanding of how semantic models connect to downstream data products, metadata catalogues, and AI/ML enrichment workflows, and the ability to assure that integration is sound. Knowledge of property graph modelling and the ability to move between RDF-based and property graph paradigms depending on platform and use case. Experience with entity resolution, semantic search, and knowledge-driven RAG architectures. Experience working within modern data architectures including data mesh, data lakehouse, and federated governance models. Background in linked data principles (W3C standards) and LLM grounding techniques, including GraphRAG and ontology-grounded generation, and practical experience applying them in enterprise contexts. Industry experience in Financial Services, Government, Health, Energy, or Utilities sectors in APAC is highly regarded. Good communication skills with the ability to engage both technical teams and business SMEs. Working knowledge of finance data structures, including chart of accounts, entity hierarchy, sub-ledger to ledger relationships, intercompany and period close, together with actual, budget and forecast data, currencies, consolidation and management hierarchies. Strong data modelling discipline and the ability to justify and maintain definitional standards, including canonical or semantic models, data contracts, schema evolution, metadata, lineage and data-quality controls. Experience extracting and reconciling data from enterprise applications or complex operational systems using APIs, files, database interfaces or change-data-capture patterns. Experience deploying software or data products on Azure, AWS or GCP, DataBricks, Snowflake, Palantir etc. using relevant cloud services and at least one of containers, Kubernetes or serverless patterns. (AI engineer – desirable) Understanding of secure data engineering, including access control, encryption, secrets, privacy, retention and the handling of sensitive or regulated data. Ability to work with finance SMEs and technical teams to translate business definitions and controls into implementable data products and acceptance criteria. Experience evaluating retrieval quality for AI workloads, including embeddings, vector stores, hybrid search or reranking. The platform provides a managed agent runtime, standardized MCP connectors to enterprise systems of record, a shared UI component library with a design system, an intelligence data/context layer and a gold-standard promotion pipeline from prototype to production.   As a Staff Product Manager , you will own the product strategy, roadmap, and execution for the Agentic Platform the foundational layer that every domain workspace depends on. You will work across agent runtime, MCP connectors, intelligence layer, evaluation framework, developer experience, and governance to deliver a platform that reduces time-to-production from months to weeks while maintaining enterprise grade quality, security, and reliability. You will partner closely with Application Engineering, the CIO organization, and domain teams across GTM, HR, Finance, and Product to ensure the platform serves real needs and scales with the organization. description: We are seeking a Semantic Architecture & Context Engineering Lead to help define and scale the semantic foundation underpinning our enterprise data, analytics, AI, and agentic ecosystem. As organizations increasingly consume data through natural-language interfaces, generative AI, intelligent agents, predictive models, and automated workflows, the quality of the underlying context becomes as important as the quality of the underlying data. Business concepts, metrics, relationships, definitions, metadata, instructions, retrieval strategies, and decision rules must be structured in ways that are consistent, machine-readable, reusable, governed, and optimized for AI consumption. This role will establish the practices, standards, and reusable patterns through which business and data context is represented across our data products, analytical models, GenAI solutions, and agent architectures. The individual will work horizontally across Data, Analytics, AI, Product, Engineering, Architecture, and business domain teams. They will partner closely with functional owners—including data product managers, AI engineers, data scientists, architects, and business subject-matter experts—to ensure semantic and contextual structures are designed consistently while remaining appropriate to individual domains and use cases. Critically, this is not solely a governance or documentation role. The Semantic Architecture & Context Engineering Lead will establish an experimental discipline around context , using structured evaluation, A/B testing, production telemetry, and AI-assisted techniques to continuously improve the accuracy, precision, reliability, performance, and usability of AI-enabled solutions. Job Responsibilities Enterprise Semantic & Context Architecture . Define the enterprise framework for representing business meaning and context across data, analytics, AI, and agentic solutions. Establish standards and reusable patterns for semantic models, business concepts, metrics, entities, relationships, taxonomies, metadata, definitions, contextual instructions, and knowledge structures. Develop a common approach for translating human business concepts into machine-readable and AI-consumable representations. Define principles for semantic interoperability across data products and domains, minimizing conflicting definitions, redundant logic, and fragmented representations of common enterprise concepts. Establish semantic and context architecture patterns that can be applied across structured, semi-structured, and unstructured information. AI & Agent Context Engineering - Define best practices for structuring the context provided to GenAI and agentic solutions, including system instructions, business rules, semantic metadata, examples, retrieval context, tool descriptions, entity relationships, and domain knowledge. Partner with AI engineering and architecture teams to design context patterns for RAG, natural-language-to-data, reasoning, agent tool use, memory, workflow orchestration, and agent-to-agent interaction. Develop reusable context architectures for solutions such as Databricks Genie spaces/rooms, enterprise AI assistants, analytical agents, and domain-specific agents. Ensure context structures clearly establish authoritative definitions, permitted sources, relationships, hierarchies, temporal logic, calculation rules, and other constraints required for reliable AI reasoning. Help establish standards for context isolation, inheritance, reuse, versioning, and lifecycle management across an expanding portfolio of AI solutions. Data Product Semantics - Partner with data product managers and domain teams to strengthen the semantic layer of enterprise data products. Establish standards for business definitions, logical models, physical-to-logical mappings, metrics, dimensions, entity relationships, metadata, lineage, data-quality expectations, and consumption guidance. Ensure data products contain sufficient semantic context for use by human analysts, BI platforms, machine-learning models, GenAI applications, and autonomous agents. Promote reusable semantic contracts that allow downstream solutions to interpret data consistently without recreating business logic independently. Identify common concepts and relationships that should be standardized across multiple data domains while preserving appropriate domain ownership. Context Experimentation & Evaluation - Establish a systematic testing framework for semantic and contextual design. Design and lead experiments to evaluate alternative context structures, instructions, examples, semantic representations, retrieval strategies, and metadata configurations. Use A/B testing, offline evaluation, golden question sets, adversarial testing, production telemetry, and other methods to measure changes in: - answer accuracy, precision and recall, grounding and source fidelity etc Semantic Lifecycle & Governance - Establish lifecycle practices for creating, reviewing, approving, versioning, testing, deploying, monitoring, and retiring semantic and contextual assets. Define ownership models distinguishing enterprise standards from domain-level business ownership. Ensure semantic assets can be traced to authoritative business definitions and trusted data sources. AI-Enabled Semantic Engineering - Identify opportunities to embed AI throughout the semantic lifecycle. Use AI-assisted techniques to accelerate metadata generation, concept extraction, taxonomy development, relationship identification, mapping, documentation, semantic validation, and quality assurance. Partnership & Adoption - Act as a subject-matter expert and internal advisor on semantic architecture and context engineering. Partner with Data Product, Data Engineering, AI/ML, Business Intelligence, Product, Design, Architecture, and business teams to embed semantic best practices into delivery. Conduct design reviews and working sessions for priority data and AI solutions. Develop playbooks, templates, education, and reusable implementation patterns that allow teams to adopt semantic practices without requiring centralized execution. Build a community of practice across data and AI teams to continuously advance enterprise capabilities. Translate highly technical semantic concepts into clear implications for product owners, executives, and business stakeholders. Required Qualifications Significant experience in one or more of the following areas: semantic architecture, data architecture, knowledge engineering, ontology development, data product management, AI/ML engineering, information architecture, or advanced analytics. Strong understanding of enterprise data architecture, including logical and physical data models, metadata, data products, metrics, dimensions, lineage, and data governance. Demonstrated understanding of modern GenAI architectures, including LLMs, RAG, vector retrieval, natural-language-to-data solutions, prompt/context engineering, and agentic architectures. Experience translating complex business concepts and domain knowledge into structured technical representations. Strong analytical orientation with experience designing experiments, evaluations, or other quantitative methods for assessing solution performance. Ability to operate effectively across business, product, data, engineering, and architecture organizations. Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to influence without direct ownership of participating teams. description: About Neo4j: Neo4j is the graph intelligence platform that transforms data into knowledge to power the next generation of intelligent applications and AI systems. It includes enterprise-ready knowledge graphs for accurate, explainable, and governed AI; the most comprehensive, trusted, and easy-to-deploy graph capabilities across any environment and data source; and an unmatched ecosystem trusted by 84 of the Fortune 100 and supported by the world’s largest graph community. Intelligence that works. Results that matter. Built to work everywhere and integrate with everything across every cloud for dynamic, personalized, and autonomous AI systems. We deliver quicker results, contextual knowledge, and solutions that impact customers and employees across the business. Our Vision:  At Neo4j, we have always strived to help the world make sense of data.   As business, society and knowledge become increasingly connected, our technology promotes innovation by helping organizations to find and understand data relationships. We created, drive and lead the graph database category, and we’re disrupting how organizations leverage their data to innovate and stay competitive. The Role: We're looking for a software engineer to join the Neo4j Sharding Engineering team. We own Infinigraph and Composite , and we make them work as managed offerings on Aura, Neo4j’s cloud platform. Aura is Neo4j’s fully managed graph database as a service. Customers create, scale, and use Neo4j databases in the cloud without installing, clustering, or operating the database themselves. Aura runs on Kubernetes across Google Cloud, AWS, and Azure, and handles provisioning, networking, security, upgrades, and day-to-day operations for those databases. Composite is the technology behind distributed query execution in Neo4j: one query can span multiple databases. Infinigraph is our database sharding offering for large data volumes, built on a distributed database architecture. Distributed query execution is a complex and interesting topic covering query language design, performant networking, and concurrency. Those capabilities still have to run as a cloud product, and that's where a large part of this role sits: building the Go services and Kubernetes machinery that provision, scale, and operate sharded and composite clusters on Aura, reliably, at the data volumes our customers keep growing into.
